healthcareSystem: Universal (National Health System / NHS — ESY for residents)
qualityNotes: Good healthcare system with decent hospitals on the mainland and islands. Major cities have excellent private hospitals. On smaller islands, healthcare is more limited. English is commonly spoken in tourist areas and private hospitals.
pharmacyHours: Most pharmacies open 8am-8pm weekdays. Each area has a rotating 'on-duty pharmacy' (φαρμακείο νυχτερινής βάρδιας) open nights and weekends — look for the sign in any pharmacy window or search online.
pharmacyTips: Pharmacies (φαρμακείο) are widely available. Many medications require a prescription. Greek pharmacists can advise on minor ailments. Look for the green cross sign. Some OTC items available without prescription.
prescriptionRules: EU prescriptions are accepted. Non-EU prescriptions require validation by a Greek doctor. Greece follows EU prescription rules — many common medications require prescriptions.

restrictedMeds.name: Codeine-containing medications
restrictedMeds.note: Codeine products require a prescription in Greece. Some codeine products may be restricted.

restrictedMeds.name: ADHD medications (Adderall, Ritalin, methylphenidate)
restrictedMeds.note: Controlled substances. A Greek prescription or special authorization may be required.

restrictedMeds.name: Benzodiazepines
restrictedMeds.note: Controlled substances requiring a prescription. Greece has strict regulations.

restrictedMeds.name: Medical cannabis
restrictedMeds.note: Cannabis is illegal in Greece for recreational use. Medical cannabis was legalized in 2018 but remains very restricted.

bringDocumentation: Carry a doctor's letter and prescription (ideally in Greek or English) for all medications. Bring sufficient supply in original packaging. For controlled substances, carry prescription documentation. EU citizens should carry the EHIC card.

travelInsurance.requiredNote: Not legally required for short stays, but strongly recommended. EU citizens should carry EHIC/GHIC.
travelInsurance.tips: Greek hospitals (especially public ones) may require upfront payment or guarantee of payment from your insurance. Private hospitals are better equipped for tourists. Ensure your insurance covers medical evacuation from islands to mainland.

vaccinations.notes: No mandatory vaccinations for travelers from most countries.

waterNotes: Tap water is generally safe to drink on the mainland. On some islands, tap water may be from tanks — bottled water is advisable on smaller islands.
foodSafetyTips: Greek food is generally very safe. Olive oil, feta cheese, lamb, and fresh vegetables are staples. Saganaki (fried cheese), souvlaki, and gyros are safe from reputable establishments. Watch out for food in very touristy areas that may sit out longer.
medicalTourismNote: Greece is developing as a medical tourism destination, particularly for dental work, cosmetic surgery, and retirement living — combining quality care with Mediterranean lifestyle.
metaDescription: Complete health & medication guide for traveling to Greece. Emergency numbers (112, 166), pharmacy tips, restricted medications, vaccination requirements, and travel insurance advice.
